messages.text: so i just got off the call with prof petrov. she wants the stage breakdown table in section 4. specifically that we resolved 99.1% of those 2946 strings without a single human touch.
that's a strong headline number. i already have the logs for that, so it's easy to extract. she didn't ask about the ablation removing the trigram stage though?
she did. she wants to see if we actually need that fuzzy match step or if the embeddings are doing all the heavy lifting anyway. i'll run it tomorrow night since the cluster is quiet.
careful with that one. remember our trigram threshold was set at >=0.6, right? if you remove it, the 4b model will see a lot more borderline cases and the latency comparison might skew.

true. i'll isolate the accuracy drop from the latency increase in the results table. also, she asked about the human eval. we need to show that our auto-accept threshold isn't just guessing, so she wants 100 strings manually checked by a human.
i can take that on. i was planning to do a qualitative review of the edge cases anyway. if i start tonight i can have the first 50 done by wednesday, which fits your deadline for the full paper.
wednesday is perfect. just use the same seed set we used for the hackathon demo so the data is consistent with what's in the repo.
agreed. i'll log every disagreement between the model and my judgment as a separate column so we can calculate the inter-rater reliability later if needed.
you're terrifyingly thorough. thanks. i'm going to go merge that retry logic for the failed jobs now, then i might actually sleep before the demo starts tomorrow.
good luck with the merge. make sure you don't push directly to main again like last time lol
i am pushing a PR. i have standards. see you tomorrow at 9 for the dry run?
yes, 9am sharp. i'll bring the dataset csv so we can double check the column headers before we start.
